I’ve just finished updating the UI code for the studio editor to make it look more like Roblox’s own interface. The changes span three key assets: `studio.js` (the main editor logic and UI layout), `icons.js` (adding the new move and scale icons referenced by the ribbon toolbar), and `site.css` (styling the top bar, side panel, canvas wrapper, etc.). 

Before I proceed further, I need to ensure that the JavaScript I just wrote is syntactically valid. A syntax error in either file would break the entire editor, and the user will likely encounter a blank screen or console errors when they load the page. Since the changes are substantial – I introduced new imports, added a large constant array, and wrote several new functions – a quick lint isn’t enough; I need the Node.js interpreter to actually parse the files. 

The most straightforward way to do this in the current environment is to use `node --check`, which parses a file without executing it. However, I can’t run `node --check` directly on the source files in their original location because the project’s build pipeline may have other side effects, and I also want to avoid interfering with any live server that might be watching those paths. A safe approach is to copy each file to a temporary location (`/tmp/check.mjs`) and run the syntax check there. I can chain the two checks together: first copy `studio.js`, run `node --check`, then overwrite the same temporary file with `icons.js` and run the check again. If both commands succeed, I’ll output a simple confirmation string like “syntax OK” so I can see the result in the tool output.

I also need to include a description for the tool call that clearly explains what I’m doing – “Syntax-check rewritten studio and icons” – so that anyone reviewing the logs understands the purpose. The command should be a single Bash invocation that performs the copy‑check‑copy‑check sequence and then echoes the success message. Using `&&` ensures that if any step fails, the subsequent steps won’t run, and the tool will return the error output, which I can then address.

Thus, the next logical step is to issue a Bash tool call with exactly this command and description. This will give me immediate feedback on whether the recent edits introduced any syntax errors before I move on to runtime testing or further UI tweaks.

arguments.command: cp public/js/studio/studio.js /tmp/check.mjs && node --check /tmp/check.mjs && cp public/js/icons.js /tmp/check.mjs && node --check /tmp/check.mjs && echo "syntax OK"
